newsitem.title: JAPAN: Japan says almost 500 hit by Qantas food poisoning.
newsitem.headline: Japan says almost 500 hit by Qantas food poisoning.

text.p: At least 480 passengers on Australian Qantas Airways aircraft flying to Japan have been hit by an outbreak of food poisoning during the past 10 days, Japan's Health Ministry said on Thursday.
A ministry spokesman told reporters 480 passengers, most of them Japanese, on several Qantas Airways flights from Cairns between November 3 and 7 had contracted food poisoning linked to their flight.
The spokesman said at least 56 needed some hospital treatment for the salmonella poisoning.
He did not give further details such as the nationality of passengers other than the Japanese.
Australian health authorities had identified "dessert sauce" served to passengers as the cause of the poisoning, he said.
A Qantas spokesman in Sydney said earlier this week the sauce was no longer being used on any Qantas flights.
Qantas Airways officials were "acting properly" and were urging passengers to consult doctors, the health ministry spokesman said.
Toshiaki Hatsuyama, Qantas' spokesman in Tokyo, told Reuters the airline had sent letters of apology to all passengers affected.
"We have received many inquiries from our customers about the food poisoning," he said.
He said Qantas had taken all necessary measures to head off future outbreaks of food poisoning.
"There are no worries (about food poisoning) any more," he said.
Qantas' Japan to Australia routes are generally seen as its most profitable.
Earlier this year, Japan was hit by its own outbreak of food poisoning which killed 11 people, mainly schoolchildren, and made 9,500 ill.
Health authorities believe school lunches caused the outbreak but were unable to pinpoint the exact ingredient.
